title: Policy Gradient with Tree Expansion
summary: Two explicit counterexamples invalidate core spectral guarantees: Theorem 4.4's C-SoftTreeMax bound fails for a positive diagonalizable kernel with simple eigenvalues; Theorem 4.7's reversible E-SoftTreeMax clause claims a faster exponential rate than the exact variance.
page_convention: Printed local pages 1-27 equal physical PDF pages; not PMLR continuous pages.

problems.title: C-SoftTreeMax's finite eigenvalue bound omits nonorthogonal spectral projections
problems.claim: Theorem 4.4 bounds Var(G_C) by 2 A^2 S^2 beta^2/(1-gamma)^2 |lambda_2(P)|^{2(d-1)}.
problems.location: PDF p.4, Theorem 4.4; pp.4-5 proof outline; Appendix A.4 pp.14-15
assumptions: Every action transition positive, minimum833/5000; row sums1
problems.suspect_step: Appendix A.4 replaces the sum of Frobenius norms of biorthogonal spectral projections by S-1, though those projections need not have unit norm.

check.argument: Gradients are +/-eta(delta u^T+v^T/6). Their mean is0 and Var=4 eta^2(2delta^2+1/6).

counterevidence: All eigenvalues distinct, so repeated-eigenvalue/Jordan caveat does not rescue statement.
Uses actual bounded MDP Q, no unrestricted-Q scaling.
Rank-one kernel special case remains valid for d>=2.
Exact trajectory sums and tabular parameters match theory.
problems.impact: Direct contradiction of first main theoretical guarantee; affects central spectral variance bound and finite-depth behavior-policy guidance. Does not establish failure of Atari scores.

correction.limits: Does not certify a complete revised algorithm or restore original eigenvalue-only constant.

result.argument: Gradients are +/-eta(delta u^T+v^T/6). Their mean is0 and Var=4 eta^2(2delta^2+1/6).

problems.title: Reversibility does not imply E-SoftTreeMax's claimed ordinary-eigenvalue rate
problems.claim: Theorem4.7 says Var(G_E)=O(beta^2 alpha^{2d}) with alpha=|lambda2(P)| if P is reversible or rewards constant.
problems.location: PDF p.5 Theorem4.7; Appendix A.8 pp.17-20, especially (31)-(32)
assumptions: Action rows P_s +/- (1/100)(1,-1,0); nonnegative rows sum1
Symmetric P, irreducible, aperiodic, uniform stationary distribution; eigenvalues1,-1/2,2/5
SoftTreeMax policy uniform for every depth; actual Q=(8/5,8/5,4/5) identical between actions
problems.suspect_step: Ordinary reversible-chain spectrum does not control reward-weighted product rate; lower bound(31) is depth-dependent, not uniform.

check.argument: Scaled products D_kP, D_k=diag(1,1,exp(-2^k)), give a_n=(a_{n-1}+b_{n-1})/2,b_n=exp(-2^n)a_{n-1}. A_n=2^na_n increases to finite positive Ainf. Antisymmetric numerator=(2/5)^n; denominator Theta((1/2)^n). Actual variance Theta((4/5)^{2d}), violating O((1/2)^{2d}).
check.finite_check: Direct scaled matrix products and central finite differences at depths2,3,5,10; recurrence diagnostics through d40.

counterevidence: Actual exponential decay still occurs with alpha=4/5; general existence assertion not refuted by this example.
Rewards nonconstant; constant-reward special case not challenged.
P symmetric with distinct eigenvalues; no nonnormality or Jordan issue.
Source theorem text and reversible OR clause confirmed by actual page5 image.
problems.impact: Refutes core reversible rate in Theorem4.7 and its transition-spectrum interpretation. Does not refute reported Atari results.

correction.limits: Removing reversible clause eliminates the directly contradicted assertion; no complete repair of general E theorem certified.

result.argument: Scaled products D_kP, D_k=diag(1,1,exp(-2^k)), give a_n=(a_{n-1}+b_{n-1})/2,b_n=exp(-2^n)a_{n-1}. A_n=2^na_n increases to finite positive Ainf. Antisymmetric numerator=(2/5)^n; denominator Theta((1/2)^n). Actual variance Theta((4/5)^{2d}), violating O((1/2)^{2d}).
result.finite_check: Direct scaled matrix products and central finite differences at depths2,3,5,10; recurrence diagnostics through d40.
